question.text: Mr. Vikram Menon, the COO of Tilak Private Credit Fund (Cat II), is comparing the regulatory status of Fund Administrator/Fund Accountant vs Custodian roles. Which statement correctly describes the Indian regulatory position?

answer.text: Both Fund Administrator and Custodian are SEBI-regulated; both need separate registration

Fund Administrator / Fund Accountant is NOT a SEBI-regulated function in India (unlike in several developed markets), whereas Custodian must be registered with SEBI under SEBI (Custodian) Regulations, 1996
Only Fund Administrator is SEBI-regulated; Custodian is self-regulated through APMI
Neither Fund Administrator nor Custodian requires any registration for Cat I/II AIFs

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that Fund Accountant / Fund Administrator is not a regulated function in India, in contrast with several developed markets where it is. All custodians of AIFs, on the other hand, must be registered with SEBI under the SEBI (Custodian) Regulations, 1996. The fund-administration function is therefore left to a commercial arrangement between the AIF and its chosen service provider, whereas custody is a SEBI-licensed activity. The Trap: The "both regulated" option wrongly extends SEBI registration to fund administration. The "only fund administrator regulated" option inverts the actual regulatory split. The "neither requires registration" option ignores the mandatory SEBI registration of custodians under the Custodian Regulations. Note: The contrast to remember is regulated custodian versus unregulated fund administrator. The workbook describes fund administration as a service that may be performed by the custodian, a third-party vendor, or in-house, but does not place it under a separate SEBI registration regime.
